questiontext.text:
Consider the diagram below:
Two GREEN angles are formed between each parallel line and the line sloping upwards.
Two BLUE angles are formed between each parallel line and the line sloping downwards.

var angleL = {#greenAngle#}; var angleR = {#blueAngle#}; var lineStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false, strokeColor:"black" }; var hatchStyle = { fixed:true, highlight:false, strokeColor:"black", face:"<" }; var angleStyle = { radius:1.5, orthoType:"sector", highlight:false, name:"\\(z^\\circ\\)", withLabel:true, label:{ highlight:false, position:"auto", offset:[-5,0], fontSize:15, strokeColor:"black" } }; var pointO = board.create("point", [0,2], {visible:false}); var pointR = board.create("point", [7,-2], {visible:false}); var pointL = board.create("point", [-7,-2], {visible:false}); var paraLineA = board.create("line", [[-4,2], [4,2]], lineStyle); var paraLineB = board.create("line", [[-4,-2], [4,-2]], lineStyle); board.create("hatch", [paraLineB, 2], hatchStyle); hatchStyle.anchor = 0.2; board.create("hatch", [paraLineA, 2], hatchStyle); var lineL = board.create("line", [[0,2], [-4/Math.tan(angleL*Math.PI/180),-2]], lineStyle); var lineR = board.create("line", [[0,2], [4/Math.tan((180-angleR)*Math.PI/180),-2]], lineStyle); var intersectionL = board.create("intersection", [paraLineB, lineL], {visible:false}); var intersectionR = board.create("intersection", [paraLineB, lineR], {visible:false}); board.create("angle", [lineL, lineR, -1, -1], angleStyle); angleStyle.strokeColor="green"; angleStyle.fillColor="green"; angleStyle.label.offset = [2,-2]; angleStyle.name = "\\(x^\\circ\\)"; board.create("angle", [paraLineA, lineL, -1, 1], angleStyle); } else if (angleDisp == -1 && angleR >= 110) { angleStyle.label.offset = [30,-8]; } else { angleStyle.label.offset = [-3,-8]; }; angleStyle.name = "\\(".concat(angleR, "^\\circ\\)"); board.create("angle", [paraLineB, lineR, -angleDisp, angleDisp], angleStyle); (a) The two GREEN angles are: [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]]

Given the lower GREEN angle is \({@greenAngle@}^\circ\), find the angle \(x^\circ\).

\(x =\) [[input:ans2]] \(^\circ\) [[validation:ans2]]

(2)

[[feedback:prt1]]


(b) The two BLUE angles are: [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]]

Given the lower BLUE angle is \({@blueAngle@}^\circ\), find the angle \(y^\circ\).

\(y =\) [[input:ans4]] \(^\circ\) [[validation:ans4]]

(2)

[[feedback:prt2]]


(c) What is the sum of the angles \(x\), \(y\) and \(z\)?

\(x + y + z =\)[[input:ans5]] \(^\circ\) [[validation:ans5]]

Hence, find the angle \(z^\circ\)

\(z =\) [[input:ans6]] \(^\circ\) [[validation:ans6]]

(2)

[[feedback:prt3]]

Angles which are {@tans1@} are equal in size.
So, \(x = {@greenAngle@}^\circ\).

You have calculated the correct value for \(x\).
However, the two green angles are {@tans1@}.
You are correct that the green angles are {@tans1@}.

You have attempted to calculate \(x\) by summing the green angles to \(180^\circ\).
However, since the two green angles are {@tans1@}, they are equal in size.

{@if tans3="consecutive" then "" else "Although, the blue angles are not themselves consecutive, the consecutive angle to \\(y\\) is a vertical angle to the lower blue angle. Therefore, the lower blue angle has the same size as the consecutive angle to \\(y\\)."@} Angles which are consecutive sum to \(180^\circ\).
So, \(y = 180 - {@blueAngle@} = {@tans4@}^\circ\).

You have calculated the correct value for \(y\).
However, the two green angles are {@tans3@}.
You are correct that the blue angles {@if tans3="consecutive" then "are consecutive" else "do not have any of the listed relationships"@}.

Here is a worked solution:

The vertical angle to \(z\) forms a straight line with the angles \(x\) and \(y\).
